hypotheses.justification: The `KeyU` section's `variable` command declares this instance. The theorem takes it as an argument only because the instance's type mentions nothing but `𝒪`, which is already an argument; neither the statement nor the proof uses it. Nothing in the statement needs it to elaborate. `AdicPoint`, `modPow`, `stdFullLattice`, `latticeBaseChange` and `DeligneDatum.line` are all defined under `[CommRing 𝒪] [Field K] [Algebra 𝒪 K]` and `[CommRing R] [Algebra 𝒪 R]` only. `coordEquiv` (`StdBasis` section, line 272) and `lineCoord` (`Levels` section, line 487) additionally need only `[IsDomain 𝒪]` and `[IsFractionRing 𝒪 K]`, which stay. The proof uses nothing from the discrete valuation ring structure. It rewrites with the definition of `lineCoord` and with `Submodule.mem_map`, then uses `LinearEquiv.coe_coe` and the injectivity of the linear equivalence `coordEquiv`. These steps hold for any linear equivalence, so the same proof compiles unchanged after `omit [IsDiscreteValuationRing 𝒪] in`.
